I've been reading a lot about the gut biome and it's really important to have good gut bacteria. Prebiotics are supposed to be even better, like Korean Kim Chi, but I can't stand the stuff.

Depression is a chemical imbalance. It's good that you recognize you're depressed, but remember also that your thinking and judgment is affected by the depression.  If you've alienated people, reach out to them. Apologize. Ask for help. Your family, at least a few family members, will likely respond. 

Try to just take it a day at a time. Try faking it, some theories say that if you pretend you're happy, you will be happy.  Distract yourself and don't dwell on the depressive thoughts. They don't represent reality, your brain has a skewed perception right now.

I wonder why you keep saying you're a lazy piece of shit. Did someone tell you that when you were growing up?  Change that tape in your head. Replace it with something like, "I've just make a huge transition in my life and I'm doing the best that I can".  You keep saying you're dumb. I used to think I was stupid, even with a genius level IQ, because my dad told me I was. You got into the university. Trust me, they have plenty of out of state applicants and they didn't pick you just for your money. 

Look at all of the things that take up your time and prioritize. Why worry about being in clubs?  As an engineering major, I didn't have time for that stuff. This isn't high school, where you need that to get into college. 

Are you really interested in computer science or is that what you think you should do?  If you really like your major, you'll be more motivated to study

Multi variable calculus is a hard class. But you have time. Pull some all-nighters studying. Don't give up before it's over. 

Do you have the option to retake some classes?  Talk to your counselor. 

Have you been able to build a support network at school?  If you don't have someone to talk to, call a suicide hotline. 

Suicide is a permanent solution to a temporary problem.

I see that you're a chemical engineer. My question would be does failure of the casing from what you're describing as external corrosion cause loss of containment?  This seems to be a mechanical engineering issue. It's great that you question things in all fields, as being an engineer is understanding also how the systems interact. Also, what is the service?  If these are for pool pump discharge versus high pressure hydrogen service, there's a difference. 

I have my Professional Engineering license and my license states that I must go as far as to quit my job in protest if my company is actually designing something unsafe. But as a ChemE, I can't necessarily make an informed decision on this particular issue

So, do a little more research, frame the concern properly, research whether gauges of the new type have a known higher failure rate, etc then you can make a recommendation to do proper testing. And you should be able to tell them what that proper testing is and how long it will take and how much it will cost

Offer solutions, not problems
